gen-gf-pangolin-bitter: Friendly one-nib letters in Pangolin, generous lowercase, wide c apertures. And Bitter holds a slab-serif column, while Pangolin belongs in a short shout of large letters.
gen-gf-pochaevsk-fs-bespoke-sans: Pochaevsk leaves every lowercase a with its mouth ajar. Bespoke Sans prefers a smaller size, a sans-serif with generous gaps at the stems, sharp and refined.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-cascadia-code: Tin-can mouths and a fixed nib: Shantell Sans, distinctive and expressive. And Cascadia Code holds a sans-serif column, while Shantell Sans lives in a short, large line.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa keeps thickness that does not change with direction, curves left wide. And Lexend Exa prefers a smaller size under Shantell Sans, whose mouths stay cut-lid wide.
gen-gf-sirin-stencil-work-sans: Drilled-glass counters and unvarying stroke thickness mark Sirin Stencil at once. And Work Sans brings open c tips and joins matching the stems, a contemporary line under that display.
gen-gf-slackey-fs-public-sans: Slackey leaves long pauses between letters, horizontals a notch lighter. Public Sans holds a stretch of sans-serif copy, hefty lowercase and broad counters on the rounds.
gen-gf-slackey-fs-ranade: Long pauses between letters mark Slackey, a sturdy lowercase, horizontals a notch lighter than the uprights. Ranade drops a point, a sans with slightly shifting weight.
gen-gf-slackey-work-sans: Expressive long pauses in Slackey, a sturdy lowercase, horizontals a notch lighter. Work Sans shows what lasts: joins matching stems under that mild thick-thin display heading.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-lexend-mega: Sniglet stops terminals short of curling back, a quiet level beat. Lexend Mega stands next to that unaccented display as a high-bodied, one-nib sans-serif with a gap in every c.
gen-gf-syne-tactile-fs-fira-sans: Syne Tactile draws a broad-nibbed stroke that never curls shut, a gentle bump to the caps. And Fira Sans brings a zero-contrast line under that display, wide s curves throughout.
gen-gf-syne-tactile-fs-merriweather-sans: Sturdy, large-looking lowercase and an e that opens clearly to the right give Merriweather Sans a clean read. Merriweather Sans prefers a smaller size under Syne Tactile, a sans below.
gen-gf-syne-tactile-general-sans: Syne Tactile never curls its broad-nibbed stroke shut on the heading. General Sans does the long line, while Syne Tactile does the short shout, a sans-serif with an x-height that fills each row.
gen-gf-syne-tactile-montserrat: Distinctive broad-nibbed strokes in Syne Tactile never curl shut at all. Montserrat prefers a smaller size, a geometric sans-serif with oversized counters and a wire-like glide.
gen-gf-syne-tactile-satoshi: A broad-nibbed stroke that never curls shut marks Syne Tactile. Satoshi holds a stretch of sans-serif copy, a soaring x-height and an e that never looks squeezed.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-sofia-sans-semi-cond: A splayed c terminal marks Tilt Neon, tube-like and constant-width. Sofia Sans Semi Condensed prefers a smaller size, a plain sans whose lowercase nearly matches the caps.
